A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, method and primary experiments. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the equations, tables, figures and complete appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression, rendering-quality, speed and ablation results on N3V and Technicolor, including detailed appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds wavelet-depth and higher-fidelity ablations plus a Light4GS comparison.

M1.justification: The proposed method retains Ex4DGS decomposition, Gaussian/SH masking, differentiated quantization, single-level Haar filtering and joint RD optimization. Appendix A details the existing loss; the deeper transforms and modified quantization settings are experimental variants, not replacements for the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate dynamic scene rendering and compression on N3V and the same five Technicolor scenes. The additional Light4GS comparison uses a different N3V subset and resolution, without establishing new dataset, domain or task coverage.

E2.justification: Light4GS moves from a related-work citation in v1 to an evaluated comparator at high-compression and high-quality operating points in v2 Appendix E/Table 8. Comparator membership in the retained primary benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds protocols crossing six compression settings with three wavelet depths, testing reduced rate-loss weight and enlarged codebooks, and retraining at 1024×768 on Light4GS's N3V subset. Tables 2–3 use a separately pretrained model, as disclosed in Appendix F. These substantially extend experimental settings while retaining the original evaluations.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds two substantive investigations: whether deeper wavelet decomposition improves RD performance, and whether rate-loss weight or codebook size offers better high-fidelity trade-offs. Tables 2–3 extend the retained opacity, wavelet-removal, pruning and storage analyses to previously untested design choices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run statistics, confidence intervals or significance tests. Appendix F explains checkpoint provenance and possible pretraining variation, but adds no statistical uncertainty estimates or repeated-run evaluation procedure.

E6.justification: Existing results remain unchanged, but Tables 2, 3 and 8 add substantial evidence. Table 3 reports 30.04 dB/14.40 MB for reduced rate-loss weight versus its own L6 control at 28.73 dB/14.05 MB. Table 8 reports higher PSNR for Light4GS, while the proposed high-compression model is smaller and faster. These are new results under separately specified conditions, not improvements over v1's original scores.

T1.justification: New Appendix A, Equations 10–12, explicitly defines the rate-loss decomposition and attribute-wise entropy and VQ sums over static and dynamic Gaussians. v1 described these components verbally. This adds limited mathematical specification without introducing a theorem, proof or changed wavelet derivation.

C1.justification: The conclusion newly claims that the compression principles can be adapted to other 4DGS models beyond Ex4DGS. The central novelty, flexible RD control and up-to-91× compression claims are retained.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly links fast-motion failures to removal of high-frequency wavelet content, extending v1's blur and pruning discussion. It also interprets the new studies as supporting single-level decomposition and rate-weight tuning, and attributes Light4GS quality differences partly to design priorities and underlying models.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code access link, detailed rate-loss specification, maximum SH degree clarification, approximately one hour each for pretraining and compression optimization, and checkpoint provenance in Appendix F. Together these substantially expand reproducibility documentation; the timing and formulation disclosures do not establish changes to the original training procedure.

R1.justification: v2 adds TeTriRF and refines distinctions from QUEEN's per-frame streaming objective and LGS's surgical specialization. Previously cited Light4GS receives a dedicated concurrent-work comparison. The broader literature survey and principal novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: Changes include localized notation explanations, expanded experimental discussion, insertion of Appendices A, E and F, updated cross-references, and a NeurIPS conference footer. Most existing prose and the main section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 2, 3 and 8 and reflows existing material around them. All ten figures and seven earlier tables are retained, with table renumbering, relocation and limited caption or formatting changes rather than a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The new ablations test previously unsupported design choices, the Light4GS comparison adds relevant comparative evidence, and Appendices A/F improve methodological transparency. These provide a clear but bounded quality gain. Different pretrained checkpoints limit cross-table comparisons, exact settings for the new rate-weight/codebook variants remain unspecified, and the added claim of adaptability to other 4DGS models is untested.
